items.title: Henry "Booker T." Glass Interview, 1962-03-22
items.q: Garnier, Wooden Joe, and Bob Anthony.

ctx.x: Saxophone. Saxophone. No. Who's playing trombone, you remember? Archie Robinson and Joe Petit. Yeah, Joe Petit played with us. You must have had some trumpet players.
Oh yeah, we had good trombone. You had Dejama Garnier. Yeah, you were good. Who else? Garnier and who else? Garnier, Wooden Joe, and Bob Anthony.
Bob Anthony. And Bob Anthony. Mm-hmm. And Bob Anthony. And Bob Anthony. And Bob Anthony. And Bob Anthony. And Bob Anthony.

items.title: Henry "Booker T." Glass Interview, 1972-05-19
items.q: That's Wooden Joe's relation, Sidney Bechet.

ctx.x: Charny Tum Tums. Well how old was Bechet when he started playing?

Oh Bechet was a young man. Bechet left. I was staying on Malibu Street and Bechet left. That's Wooden Joe's relation, Sidney Bechet. He sent Wooden Joe his client from away. Wooden Joe had client heads. That's Wooden Joe's uncle I believe, Bechet. Sidney Bechet. He wasn't as old as Wooden Joe. Oh no. His nephew. His nephew. Yeah. No he wasn't as old as Joe. And we got Paul, Paul, Bonds had some brothers, Boos, they was playing. Paul Bonds. And Mealy Bonds' uncle. What did Boos play? Boos was playing Clownet. Who…

about him playing. Yeah. He played. He used to play at the Plum playing with us. That's funny. I never did know anything about him as well as I know him. Yeah Boos. Oh one more thing about the riverfront. Did you ever see anybody down there playing any music?
